newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up on active foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up on active foreign buying.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended sharply up on Thursday on the back of active foreign buying of various blue chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.87 points, or 1.05 percent, to close at 565.56 points after it fell to 559.42 points in early trade. Gainers led losers by 57 to 51, with 47 counters steady.
"After made gains today, I think market is likely to be mixed on Friday as profit taking likely to overshadowi the trade," one foreign broker said.
But some brokers said they expected the market to continue its gains on Friday because of the continuing positive news about corporate actions available in the market.
Brokers said active foreign buying boosted overall market sentiment as overseas interests seemed to ignore the news of a possible hike in the U.S interest rates.

"I think market has already made up their own figures, so I don't think it will have much impact in Jakarta. Anyway, prevailing prices of blue-chips stocks are already at the bottom," one analyst from a local securities house said.

Feedmill firm Anwar Sierad topped the active list with 9.9 million shares, rising 150 rupiah to 2,425 rupiah on what brokers said was speculative buying after news that a subsidiary planned to soon float shares.
Lippo Life, Lippo Securities and Lippo Bank of Lippo Group were the target of both foreign and local buying since the opening, brokers said.
They said market talk that the conglomerate's restructuring plan for the three financial subsidiaries was likely to succeed had prompted the active trade.
Astra was also actively sought as it rose 175 rupiah to 3,125 rupiah on talk that another conglomerate was likely to buy a stake in the widely-diversified company.
